3.4. Attendance
 
3.4.1. Students are expected to attend all classes in courses for which the y are 
registered at the University.
3.4.2. Penalties, as set forth in relevant internal documents of the University, 
will be applied if attendance falls below that stated in course sylla bi or Handbooks. 
Students are required to be present at the beginning of the semester or term and to 
remain until the semester or term is completed (which includes final examinations). 
3.4.3. Students who do not attend classes from the first day may be penalized 
or dropped from the class, in accordance with relevant Handbooks. An exception may 
be made for justifiable reasons. 
3.4.4. Students who exceed the maximum number of absences in the current 
and previous semester or term, as defined in the Handbook, will not be eligibl e for 
University-sponsored study abroad programs or other University-sponsored events.
3.4.5. At the start of each academic period, the course instructor is responsible 
for informing students in the course documentation of the attendance rules, its impact 
on their learning opportunities, and on their potential grade. Faculty have t he right to 
initiate a drop/withdrawal from a course if there is a violation of the attendance rules.
3.4.6. Only the instructor may approve a student’s request to be absent from 
class. In the event of a dispute, the matter may be reported to the Vi ce Dean or the 
authorized  official  of  the  School.  The  determination  of  the  Vice  Dean  or  t he 
authorized official of the School shall be final. 
3.4.7.  Full-time  undergraduate  students  are  required  to  be  present  in 
Kazakhstan throughout the duration of their academic program, unless the School 
Dean has granted permission for off-site research or personal trips of up to 6 (six)  
months in total during their studies, or the student has an approved leave of absence, 
subject to the University’s regulations. Violation of this condition may result in 
dismissal of the student from the University, with the exception for those approved 
for joint/dual degree programs, academic mobility, and approved internships.

formal declaration of a  primary  major by the end of their first year of study in 
accordance  with  procedures  specified  in  the  Handbook.   All  students  must  be 
accepted into the primary major no later than the end of their se cond year of study at 
the  University.  Organization  and  coordination  of  the  primary  major  declaration 
process fall under the duties of AAO.

second year of study, the student is subject to dismissal from the University. Student s 
will receive support to facilitate the declaration of their primary ma jor. Failure to 
declare the primary major may result in dismissal from the University.     
3.5.3. The declaration of the primary major is processed through the “Primary 
Major  Declaration  Form” located in SIS. The form is submitted by a student with

3.6. Declaration of Minors and Secondary Majors
 
3.6.1. Minors must be declared, the latest, by the end of the first semester of the 
student’s last year, upon approval by the Dean or School’s authorized official. Minors 
do not provide priorities for course registration. The “Minor Declaration Form”  is 
located in SIS and submitted by a student with further requirement of final approval 
by the Dean or the School’s authorized official.
3.6.2. Secondary major. The program of study for a secondary major consists 
of courses required to meet the degree requirements for each of the two ma jors, 
together with the other courses needed to meet the general education.
If  there  is  a  difference  in  the  overall  number  of  credits  required  for  the 
completion  of  the  degree  between  the  two  major  programs,  the  larger  credit 
requirement will apply. Each School shall adopt rules governing the declaration of

3.15. Calculation of GPA and CGPA
 
3.15.1. Total grade (quality) points are calculated by multiplying the number of 
credits by the grade (quality) points of the grade awarded for each course.
3.15.2. The GPA for one academic period is computed by dividing the sum of 
the earned grade points by the total graded credits attempted in this period. 
The CGPA is computed by dividing the sum of the earned grade points by the

3.33. Double, Joint/Dual, and Consecutive Degrees
 
3.33.1. This section outlines the policies and procedures governing Double, 
Joint/Dual, and Consecutive Degree programs of the University. These programs are 
designed  to  enhance  academic  collaboration  and  provide  students  with  diverse 
educational opportunities.
The specific terms, requirements, and academic provisions for each program 
may be determined and formalized in separate agreements between the University 
and the respective partner institutions and/or appropriate decisions of the authoriz ed 
official/body.
3.33.2. Double Degrees.
A Double Degree program allows students to earn two distinct degrees from 
either  University  or  in  collaboration  with  another  institution.  This  may  involve 
completing two separate theses or a single thesis that meets the require ments of both 
institutions.
Students must fulfill the specific requirements set by each institution involved.
A formal agreement must be established between the institutions outlining 
shared learning outcomes, assessment methods, and credit allocation.
Clear policies regarding credit transfer must be developed to prevent double 
counting of ECTS credits.
A comprehensive curriculum map must be created to outline which courses 
will be taken at each institution (or department) and specify learning outcomes for 
each course.
Any shared courses must be clearly defined in terms of their contribution to  
each degree's learning outcomes.
3.33.3. Joint/Dual Degrees.
A  Joint/Dual  Degree  program  requires  students  to  complete  a  unified 
curriculum that integrates courses from both institutions (or departments within t he 
University) and receive one joint/dual diploma.
A formal agreement is necessary to ensure that all learning outcomes are met 
and assessments are standardized across institutions.
The curriculum must be designed collaboratively, ensuring that all courses 
contribute to the learning outcomes of both degrees without overlap.
Agreements must comply with national educational regulations and outline 
responsibilities regarding intellectual property rights related to joint/dual research 
projects or theses.
